+## Design
+
+1. **Registrar.** `KL_srp_domain` keeps one bit for the Registrar of its declared value
+   (1 = IN, 0 = MT or LV). LV is folded into MT: sJ encodes the two alike (10.7.6.3), and
+   nothing else reads the Domain registration (35.2.4 gives the Domain no MAP; an adopted
+   Domain is kept until LINK_DOWN, F10.2). So no leavetimer and no timer slot are added.
+
+   | Event for the declared value | Registrar | Re-join |
+   |---|---|---|
+   | received New, JoinIn or JoinMt | IN | JoinIn |
+   | received Lv | IN to MT at once (Milan 4.2.7.2.2) | JoinMt |
+   | LeaveAll on the Domain lane (received) or the own sLA | IN to LV | JoinMt until re-declared |
+   | LINK_UP (Begin!), LINK_DOWN (Flush!) | MT | JoinMt |
+   | adoption of a received value | that value's registration (IN unless its Lv came first) | JoinIn / JoinMt |
+
+   Events of other values do nothing; received In/Mt never register (Table 10-4 has no such
+   row). A received event wins over a LeaveAll in the same clock, as the stream registrars
+   do (10 6.5).
+2. **Hand-over timing.** The code is chosen when the re-join is handed to the encoder.
+   `periodic!` and the own LeaveAll (its sLA comes on the round's tx! clock) hand over at
+   once, exactly as on main. A LeaveAll outside a tx! clock is a received one; its re-join
+   waits for the next tx! (`KL_srp_top`'s `join_fsm_w`), the drain it would have reached
+   anyway, so a peer's Domain declaration later in its LeaveAll MRPDU registers first.
+   A first version issued every re-join at tx!; it moved each periodic re-join one
+   T-MRP-JOIN later (the periodic expiry follows the join expiry in the same millisecond)
+   and failed srp_top N12, O1, O2 and O7, whose own-LeaveAll timelines rest on the main
+   timing. It was replaced before the commit; no record below is from it.
+3. **Own LeaveAll is JoinMt.** 10.7.6.6 / Table 10-4 txLA! take the Registrar to LV at
+   the sLA, so the re-join in the own LeaveAll MRPDU is JoinMt; the next one is JoinIn again
+   once the peer re-declares. This is the 10.7.6.3 reading; an owner who wants JoinIn there
+   would be asking for an exception to the clause.
+4. **Single New** at startup and LINK_UP is unchanged (D1, D9, DR11, srp_top 0, pp_top S1/DV2/DV6).

+## Behaviour: what is encoded when
+
+- No peer Domain: every periodic and LeaveAll re-join is JoinMt (DR1, D2, D3, DJ1, Q2).
+- Peer declaring the same Domain: JoinIn (DR2, DJ2); a bridge LeaveAll MRPDU that
+  re-declares its Domain: JoinIn (DR3, DJ3).
+- Own LeaveAll: JoinMt (DR4, F1); back to JoinIn after the peer re-declares (DR5).
+- Peer withdrawal (Lv): JoinMt from the next re-join on (DR6, DJ4); an Lv of another
+  value changes nothing (DR7).
+- A re-join already handed to the encoder keeps its code; it waits at most one T-MRP-JOIN.

+[A648] MSRP Domain re-join: JoinIn only while the declared Domain is registered, JoinMt otherwise (#184)
+
+Closes #184
+
+## What was wrong
+
+`KL_srp_domain` encoded every periodic and LeaveAll re-declaration of the Class A Domain as
+JoinIn and never looked at a Domain registration. IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7.6.3 (sJ) encodes
+JoinIn only while the Registrar of the attribute is IN, and JoinMt in MT or LV. With no
+other station declaring a Domain, the re-join must be JoinMt.
+
+## What changes
+
+- `hdl/srp/KL_srp_domain.sv` keeps a one-bit Registrar for its declared value. A received
+  New, JoinIn or JoinMt of that value sets IN. Its Lv clears IN at once (Milan v1.2
+  4.2.7.2.2, the instantaneous IN to MT). A LeaveAll, received on the Domain lane or the
+  own sLA, clears IN to LV. LINK_UP and LINK_DOWN clear it. An adoption carries the adopted
+  value's registration. LV is folded into MT, because sJ encodes the two alike and nothing
+  else reads the Domain registration (802.1Q-2018 35.2.4: no MAP for the Domain). So no
+  leavetimer is added.
+- The re-join is JoinIn if the Registrar is IN, JoinMt otherwise. Periodic and
+  own-LeaveAll re-joins are made pending at once, as before. A received LeaveAll's re-join
+  waits for the next MSRP tx! opportunity, so a bridge that re-declares its Domain after
+  its LeaveAll in the same MRPDU is normally answered JoinIn (a received LeaveAll on a tx!
+  clock, or a tx! inside the peer's MRPDU, gives JoinMt, as sJ gives for the LV Registrar
+  at that tx!). When a pending re-join is serviced, the code is snapshotted from the
+  previously registered state into the Domain event queue. That queued event keeps its
+  encoding until the encoder accepts it, also if a peer event arrives while it waits, and
+  encoder or TX backpressure can extend the drain. The single New at startup and LINK_UP
+  is unchanged.
+- `hdl/srp/KL_srp_top.sv` drives two new inputs of `KL_srp_domain`: the Domain Lv strobe
+  from the decoder, and the tx! opportunity (`join_fsm_w`).
+- No register-map change. No top-level port or parameter change: `protocol_processor_top`
+  and `KL_srp_top` keep their ports and parameters. `KL_srp_domain` gains two inputs.
+
+## Tests
+
+- `tb/srp_encoder` DR1 to DR11 (12 checks, with DR3a): no peer gives JoinMt; a peer
+  declaring gives JoinIn; a peer LeaveAll followed by its Domain before tx! gives JoinIn;

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# campaigns.sh <tag> <tree> [jobs]: every campaign that builds a changed file, in order,
+# each via gate.sh (log + rc per campaign); outputs under out/<tag>/.
+set -u
+tag="$1"; tree="$2"; jobs="${3:-3}"
+G=<scratch>/r2/bin/gate.sh
+O=<scratch>/r2/out/$tag
+rm -rf "$O"; mkdir -p "$O"
+run() { local name="$1" dir="$2"; shift 2; "$G" "$tag-camp-$name" "$tree/$dir" "$@"; }
+run srp_top        tb/srp_top    python3 mutants.py --output "$O/srp_top" --jobs "$jobs"
+run srp_admission  tb/srp_admission python3 mutants.py --output "$O/srp_admission" --jobs "$jobs"
+run aecp           tb/pp_top     python3 aecp_mutants.py --output "$O/aecp" --jobs "$jobs"
+run aecp_dispatch  tb/pp_top     python3 aecp_dispatch_mutants.py --output "$O/aecp_dispatch" --verilator verilator --jobs "$jobs"
+run ctr            tb/pp_top     python3 ctr_mutants.py --output "$O/ctr" --jobs "$jobs"
+run notify         tb/pp_top     python3 notify_mutants.py --output "$O/notify" --verilator verilator --jobs "$jobs"
+run gsi            tb/pp_top     python3 gsi_mutants.py --output "$O/gsi" --verilator verilator --jobs "$jobs"
+run name_wr        tb/pp_top     python3 name_wr_mutant.py --output "$O/name_wr"
+run acmp           tb/pp_top     python3 acmp_mutants.py --output "$O/acmp" --verilator verilator --jobs "$jobs"
+run d3             tb/pp_top     python3 d3_mutants.py --output "$O/d3" --verilator verilator --jobs "$jobs"
+run adp            tb/adp_engine python3 mutants.py --output "$O/adp" --jobs "$jobs"
+run maap           tb/maap       python3 mutants.py --output "$O/maap" --jobs "$jobs"
+run name_state     tb/name_state python3 mutants.py --output "$O/name_state" --verilator verilator --jobs 2
+run elab_mutants   tb/elab_guards python3 -B mutants.py --output "$O/elab_mutants" --verilator verilator --jobs "$jobs"
+echo "campaigns $tag done"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# compare_out.sh <campaign>: per-arm receipts in out/base/<c> vs out/head/<c>; compares each
+# common receipt's sorted failing-check lines (FAIL ...), and lists receipts present on one side
+c="$1"; B=<scratch>/r2/out/base/$c; H=<scratch>/r2/out/head/$c
+[ -d "$B" ] && [ -d "$H" ] || { echo "$c: missing output dir"; exit 1; }
+common=0; same=0; diffs=()
+while IFS= read -r rel; do
+  [ -f "$H/$rel" ] || continue
+  common=$((common + 1))
+  if diff -q <(grep -E '(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL[: ]' "$B/$rel" | sed -E 's/(all\.v|sim_main\.cpp|\.sv|\.cpp|\.hpp):[0-9]+/\1:N/g' | sort) \
+             <(grep -E '(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL[: ]' "$H/$rel" | sed -E 's/(all\.v|sim_main\.cpp|\.sv|\.cpp|\.hpp):[0-9]+/\1:N/g' | sort) > /dev/null; then
+    same=$((same + 1))
+  else
+    diffs+=("$rel")
+  fi
+done < <(cd "$B" && find . -type f \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.json' \) | sort)
+onlyb=$(comm -23 <(cd "$B" && find . -type f | sort) <(cd "$H" && find . -type f | sort) | wc -l)
+onlyh=$(comm -13 <(cd "$B" && find . -type f | sort) <(cd "$H" && find . -type f | sort) | wc -l)
+echo "$c: $common common receipts, $same identical failing sets; only-base $onlyb, only-head $onlyh; differing: ${diffs[*]:-none}"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# domain_area.sh <tree> <workdir>: KL_srp_domain alone, sv2v 0.0.12 then Yosys synth_xilinx
+# (xc7, flattened); the Yosys run is in <workdir> so its scratch files stay out of every tree
+set -eu
+tree="$1"; w="$2"
+export PATH="<tools>/sv2v-v0.0.12:$PATH"
+rm -rf "$w"; mkdir -p "$w"
+sv2v --version; yosys -V
+sha256sum "$tree/hdl/srp/KL_srp_domain.sv"
+sv2v "$tree/hdl/srp/KL_srp_domain.sv" > "$w/KL_srp_domain.v"
+cd "$w"
+yosys -q -p "read_verilog KL_srp_domain.v; synth_xilinx -family xc7 -flatten -top KL_srp_domain; tee -o stat.txt stat" > yosys.log 2>&1
+grep -E '^ +[0-9]+ +(FD|LUT)' stat.txt
+awk '$2 ~ /^FD/ {f+=$1} $2 ~ /^LUT/ {l+=$1} END {print "FF", f, "LUT", l}' stat.txt

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# gate.sh <log-name> <workdir> <command...>
+# Runs one gate with the pinned tools, never piped; writes <log>.log and <log>.rc.
+set -u
+name="$1"; dir="$2"; shift 2
+logs=<scratch>/r2/logs
+mkdir -p "$logs"
+export PATH="<tools>/pinned-verilator-5.050:<tools>/sv2v-v0.0.12:$PATH"
+if [ -n "${GATE_VENV:-}" ]; then export PATH="$GATE_VENV/bin:$PATH"; fi
+rm -f "$logs/$name.rc"
+{
+  echo "## gate $name"
+  echo "## dir $dir"
+  echo "## cmd $*"
+  echo "## head $(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)"
+  echo "## start $(date -Is)"
+} > "$logs/$name.log"
+cd "$dir" || { echo 99 > "$logs/$name.rc"; exit 99; }
+"$@" >> "$logs/$name.log" 2>&1
+rc=$?
+echo "## end $(date -Is) rc $rc" >> "$logs/$name.log"
+echo "$rc" > "$logs/$name.rc"
+exit "$rc"

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gen_index.py <dir>: write <dir>/INDEX.md from the files present under <dir>: path,
+bytes, sha256, and for gate logs the command, start and rc read from the log itself."""
+import hashlib, re, sys
+from pathlib import Path
+root = Path(sys.argv[1])
+rows = []
+for p in sorted(x for x in root.rglob("*") if x.is_file() and x.name != "INDEX.md"):
+    data = p.read_bytes()
+    note = ""
+    if p.suffix == ".log":
+        text = data.decode(errors="replace")
+        cmd = re.search(r"^## cmd (.*)$", text, re.M)
+        end = re.search(r"^## end (\S+) rc (\d+)$", text, re.M)
+        if cmd:
+            note = f"`{cmd.group(1)}`"
+        if end:
+            note += f"; rc {end.group(2)}, ended {end.group(1)}"
+    elif p.suffix == ".rc":
+        note = f"rc {data.decode().strip()}"
+    rows.append(f"| `{p.relative_to(root)}` | {len(data)} | `{hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}` | {note} |")
+out = ["# Round-2 receipts index", "",
+       f"Generated by `bin/gen_index.py` from the {len(rows)} files present in this directory.",
+       "Host paths in published copies are replaced by `<scratch>`, `<lane>`, `<tools>`, `<home>`.",
+       "", "| file | bytes | sha256 | gate command; rc (from the file) |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
+(root / "INDEX.md").write_text("\n".join(out + rows) + "\n")
+print(f"INDEX.md: {len(rows)} files")

+# norm.sh <log>: strip run-specific noise (headers, wall times, temp paths, tool timing lines, pin SHAs)
+grep -v '^## ' "$1" \
+ | grep -v -E 'Walltime|^- V e r i l a t i o n|Verilator: Built from|ccache|^g\+\+ |^make\[[0-9]+\]: (Entering|Leaving)' \
+ | sed -E 's#/tmp/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+#<TMP>#g; s/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ?(s|ms|sec|seconds)\b/<T>/g; s/in [0-9.]+s/in <T>/g; s/(5addf29759a22372ed6aa3e1d52a3aad29e3ecd7|88cb206135c23eb86488ad110fe19cfca5f341cf)/<PIN>/g; s/[0-9]+m[0-9.]+s/<T>/g; s/elapsed[ =:][^ ]+/elapsed=<T>/g'

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# procgates.sh <tag> <tree> <export>: the processor gates other than run_suites.sh, in order, via gate.sh
+set -u
+tag="$1"; tree="$2"; exp="$3"
+G=<scratch>/r2/bin/gate.sh
+"$G" "$tag-lint"   "$tree" ./scripts/lint_hdl.sh
+GATE_VENV=<scratch>/venv-wd "$G" "$tag-check" "$tree" make check
+"$G" "$tag-matrix" "$tree" python3 scripts/gen_matrix.py --check
+"$G" "$tag-yosys"  "$tree" ./syn/yosys/run.sh
+"$G" "$tag-guards" "$exp" python3 -B tb/elab_guards/guards.py --frontend yosys --jobs 4
+echo "procgates $tag done"

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""publish.py <dest> <src>=<rel> ...: copy each scratch file to <dest>/<rel>, with host
+paths replaced by placeholders (<scratch>, <lane>, <tools>, <home>); refuses files over
+200 KB after redaction."""
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+SUBS = [("<scratch>", "<scratch>"), ("<lane>", "<lane>"),
+        ("<tools>", "<tools>"), ("<home>", "<home>"), ("<data>", "<data>")]
+dest = Path(sys.argv[1])
+for arg in sys.argv[2:]:
+    src, rel = arg.split("=", 1)
+    data = Path(src).read_bytes()
+    for a, b in SUBS:
+        data = data.replace(a.encode(), b.encode())
+    if len(data) > 200 * 1024:
+        sys.exit(f"refused: {src} is {len(data)} bytes")
+    out = dest / rel
+    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    out.write_bytes(data)
+print(f"published {len(sys.argv) - 2} files")

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""regen_patches.py <repo> <scratch> <patch>...: rewrite each one-file patch against the
+repo's working file: its old comment text is updated, it is applied with git apply in a
+scratch copy, and the hunk is re-emitted with difflib (a/ b/ headers, no index line)."""
+import difflib, shutil, subprocess, sys
+from pathlib import Path
+OLD_C = "// periodic!, or the own sLA on its tx!"
+NEW_C = "// periodic!, or a LeaveAll on a tx! clock (own sLA)"
+repo, scratch = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
+for p in map(Path, sys.argv[3:]):
+    text = p.read_text().replace(OLD_C, NEW_C)
+    rel = next(l[6:] for l in text.splitlines() if l.startswith("+++ b/"))
+    work = scratch / p.stem
+    shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
+    (work / rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True)
+    shutil.copy(repo / rel, work / rel)
+    tmp = scratch / (p.stem + ".in.patch")
+    tmp.write_text(text)
+    subprocess.run(["git", "apply", "--check", str(tmp)], cwd=work, check=True)
+    subprocess.run(["git", "apply", str(tmp)], cwd=work, check=True)
+    src = (repo / rel).read_text().splitlines(True)
+    dst = (work / rel).read_text().splitlines(True)
+    out = "".join(difflib.unified_diff(src, dst, f"a/{rel}", f"b/{rel}", n=3))
+    p.write_text(out)
+    print(f"rewrote {p.name}")
